newsitem.title: MOROCCO: SOCCER-MOROCCO ROMPS TO FRANCE '98 WORLD CUP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MOROCCO ROMPS TO FRANCE '98 WORLD CUP.

text.p: A well-trained side of Moroccan professional footballers beat Ghana 1-0 on Saturday to qualify for the World Cup tournament in France next year.

"It is a great victory...Now the path is opened for our national team to attend the World Cup tournament in France," shouted an excited Moroccan television commentator as the match came to an end at the 90,000-capacity Mohammed V stadium in Casablanca.
"Morocco's team deserved its tickect to France...Spectators also enjoyed a high quality soccer match," Morocco trainer Henri Michel said.
Morocco opened the scoring in the 77th minute as midfielder Khalid Raghib hit a loose ball that Ghana's goalkeeper Addo Simon had no chance of stopping.
At half time the score stood at 0-0.
The Moroccans, all professional footballers including some playing with European clubs, performed agressivelu to break Ghana's strong defence wall.
Before Saturday's match, Morocco had 10 points in group five African World Cup. Ghana had a distant six points.
It was the fourth time that Morocco has qualified for the World Cup. Morocco qualified in 1970, 1986 and 1994 for the tournaments which took place twice in Mexico and in the United States.
The performance of the Atlas Lions, as the Moroccan national team is known, is a tribute to the French trainer and technical adviser Henri Michel, a Moroccan spectator said.
Hundreds of youngsters took to the streets in Casablanca and Rabat chanting slogans.
"Tonight is a real feast...We should celebrate this victory and express support to our national team," a young supporter told Moroccan RTM radio.
Security forces were deployed in the four-million-strong city of Casablanca and also in the capital, Rabat, to prevent disturbances and keep traffic rolling.
